cases.name: Qualify a lead (Send Appointment)
cases.steps: Overview -> TEST-Lead-01 Thornbury -> View -> Send Appointment
cases.ui: Banner: 'Lead qualified. Inquiry form email queued for champika.dilshan+tc101@lex-ops.io.' Pending Leads 1 -> 0.
cases.db: screening bf5cd79e status pending -> qualified at 10:56:26.418673Z. New forms row fb895055-a811-4942-ad5c-6c3d18a50de4: status=appointment_sent, client_name=TEST-Lead-01 Thornbury, client_email matches, progress_pct=0, person_responsible=Champika Dilshan, screening_id links back to the lead, unique_link=284fc353b838488e80526878a5e93b24. Created at the same microsecond as the status change.
cases.verdict: The screening update and the form creation share one timestamp, so the RPC is atomic — a half-qualified lead is not possible. Every field carried across correctly.

cases.name: Inquiry email actually reaches the client
cases.steps: Checked the Make scenario that serves SEND_INQUIRY_FORM_WEBHOOK after qualifying
cases.evidence: Scenario 'Inquiry Form Sending' (id 9795622) is INACTIVE. Its execution list for the qualify window is empty. Also inactive: 'Intake Form Sending' (9795689), 'Send Back Form' (9799068), 'Sending Intake Form' (9688858). Only 'Sending Reminders (3D, 1W, 2W)' (9690677) is active.
cases.verdict: The app did its part — it posted to the webhook and honestly reported 'queued'. Make accepted the request but will not process it while the scenario is switched off, so no email leaves. The client never receives the link.

observations.title: RPC 404 is misleading when diagnosing
observations.detail: Calling lead_email_in_use or qualify_lead with no arguments returns HTTP 404, which reads as 'function missing'. PostgREST matches functions by argument name, so a zero-arg call finds no overload. Called correctly both exist and return NOT_AUTHORISED to a non-lawyer caller. Worth knowing before anyone reports the qualify RPC as missing.

observations.title: New Lead modal takes time to mount
observations.detail: Clicking New Lead and typing immediately sent the text into the Pending Intake search box behind the modal instead. Only a nuisance for automated testing, but a fast human could hit it too. Not raised as a defect.

observations.title: Runbook used the wrong button labels
observations.detail: The lead detail modal offers 'Disqualify' and 'Send Appointment'. The runbook said 'Reject' and 'Qualify'. Same actions, different words. Runbook corrected.

observations.title: Rejected leads live under Deprioritized, not their own tab
observations.detail: Leads page has Pending and Deprioritized tabs; Deprioritized then splits into All / Rejected. Not wrong, but worth knowing when looking for a rejected lead.

observations.title: Every client-facing email scenario is switched off in Make
observations.detail: Inquiry Form Sending, Intake Form Sending, Send Back Form and Sending Intake Form are all inactive. Only the reminders scenario is on. Until they are activated no client receives an inquiry link, an intake link, or a send-back notice — which blocks stages 3 to 6 of this plan end to end, because the client cannot reach either form. The app is not at fault and its 'queued' wording is accurate.

observations.title: Webhook-to-scenario mapping was inferred by name
observations.detail: SEND_INQUIRY_FORM_WEBHOOK holds a hook URL that is only set in Vercel, so the scenario it targets could not be read directly. The match to 'Inquiry Form Sending' is by name and by the absence of any other scenario executing at that moment. Worth confirming in Make when activating.

observations.title: React needs a dispatched MouseEvent, not .click()
observations.detail: Automating the lead modal, element.click() did not open it; dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('click', {bubbles:true})) did. Only relevant to whoever automates this next.
